body.subject: Cutover trial watch: the #608 landing, its push and its report loop all verify; no Bend2 defect in the four watched classes

items.change: Read-only inspection of the live trial (state/trial.db, state/trial.db.root.log, state/trial.db.trial/, and git reads in its repo; nothing written and no baton2 run against its database). The #608 chain is correct end to end: land-checked answered {'status':'landed','target':'bend2-trial','commit':'22f0947eb4bb2df50ea4a65c16a77b197b6e22de'}, the trial worktree's bend2-trial is that same commit, and origin/bend2-trial advertises the same commit by ls-remote - so the landing verdict is not wrong and the push did not fail.
items.test: sqlite3 -readonly state/trial.db "SELECT id,sender,kind,length(body),coalesce(receipt,'NULL') FROM messages"; git -C repo ls-remote origin refs/heads/bend2-trial; git -C repo rev-parse bend2-trial
items.evidence: landed 22f0947e stated by land-checked, held by the target branch, and advertised by the remote

items.change: No report was lost and the completion signal works: the worker's report issue-608-reclaim-turn-1 carries a receipt (the root acknowledged it), and the root's review and landing reports to the operator are the only rows with a null receipt, which is by design since the operator is a terminal session with no adapter to acknowledge them. One observation on report quality, not a defect: the worker ended its turn on tool calls with no closing prose, so the documented fallback stored the terminal envelope as the report body; the root's own review then worked from the commit, and nothing was lost.
items.test: sqlite3 -readonly state/trial.db "SELECT seq,id,sender,recipient,kind,substr(body,1,80),coalesce(receipt,'NULL') FROM messages ORDER BY seq"
items.evidence: issue-608-reclaim-turn-1 has a receipt; root-to-operator reports are the null ones; the body of the worker report is the agent_end envelope because the turn produced no prose

items.change: The one operational risk the live run shows, reported without a mechanism: the running #379 turn's native log is 145327063 bytes over 14008 lines (average 10374 per line, maximum 103485), because the harness's events restate the accumulated conversation; the log had stopped growing when measured, the supervisor process is alive, and the same measurement is a harness verbosity fact rather than a coordinator fault - the coordinator retains the native log by contract. Two workers at this size are affordable; a trial of many turns accumulates gigabytes, so the standing instructions or the launcher are where a bound belongs, and none has failed yet.
items.evidence: lines=14008 bytes=145327063 avg=10374 max=103485; 0 bytes grew over a 5 s sample; the turn process and its omp child are alive

items.change: No stalled supervisor: the live turn process ('baton2 ... turn issue-379-read ...') and its omp child are running, the worker is inside a bash tool call with a 300 s timeout, and its event log is being written - the pause in the log is a tool call in flight, not a stall.
items.evidence: the turn process and /opt/homebrew/bin/omp --mode rpc ... both listed; the log stopped growing while the tool call runs

environmentRed: Nothing was run against the trial: its database was read with sqlite3 -readonly, its logs and repo were read only, and no baton2, landing or push was executed by this seat. The deployment verification command (npm test --prefix impl) is not run by this seat outside swarm integrate.

carriedForward: Watch items with no defect yet: a many-turn trial accumulates gigabytes of native logs (harness verbosity; the coordinator retains them by contract), and a worker that ends on tool calls with no prose leaves the root to read the envelope and the commit.
If the trial later shows a real failure in the four watched classes, the fix belongs in bend2-rewrite and I will take it, on the same evidence standard the last two rulings set.
